key_insight: In noisy ground-state preparation, no single quantum algorithm wins everywhere: adiabatic methods are strongest in the trivial phase, while multi-frequency cooling becomes more effective in the topological phase where gap closing hurts adiabatic evolution.
engineering_relevance: The paper gives a practical benchmarking framework for choosing and hardening noisy quantum state-preparation protocols based on Hamiltonian phase, noise rate, and hardware imperfections.
method: Analytically study an exactly solvable quadratic fermionic Hamiltonian under depolarizing noise.
Compare representative adiabatic, cooling, and QAOA-style optimization protocols for relative energy scaling.
Validate the theory with numerical simulations across phases separated by a quantum phase transition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports derived scaling laws for achievable relative energy versus noise rate, supported by numerical simulations and comparative performance across trivial and topological phases.
watch_item: Results are model-specific to an exactly solvable quadratic fermionic system with depolarizing noise, so hardware performance may differ for more general Hamiltonians and noise channels.
paper_title: Benchmark of quantum algorithms for ground state preparation in the presence of noise
